39203-an-edinburgh-eleven-pencil-portrai.title: Pencil Portraits from College Life
39203-an-edinburgh-eleven-pencil-portrai.creator: J. M. Barrie
39203-an-edinburgh-eleven-pencil-portrai.description: A book by J. M. Barrie. eral played at horses, and the Tory at running off with other boys' caps. Lord Randolph was the more distinguished at the university. One day a proctor ran him down in the streets smoking in his cap and gown. The undergraduate remarked on the changeability of the weather, but the proctor, gasping at such bravado, demanded his name and college.

67483-the-life-and-work-of-william-tinda.title: William Tindale
67483-the-life-and-work-of-william-tinda.creator: Unknown
67483-the-life-and-work-of-william-tinda.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Can we picture to ourselves the world in which Tindale gradually came into public view, made his voice heard in palaces, manor houses and homes of the common people; making enemies rage, but winning friends innumerable, until finally a price was set on his head: and there were Englishmen eager to entrap him to his death?

74869-staffordshire-pottery-and-its-hist.title: Its History
74869-staffordshire-pottery-and-its-hist.creator: Josiah C. Wedgwood, M.P., C.C.
74869-staffordshire-pottery-and-its-hist.description: A book by Josiah C. Wedgwood, M.P., C.C.. In no country is there a district so utterly associated with one trade as is the North Staffordshire Potteries. One even speaks of the Potteries in the singular as of a pure place-name. If you spoke in Timbuctoo or California of the Potteries, none could doubt that you were thinking of North Staffordshire.

arxiv-2102-07472.title: DAC: Deep Autoencoder-based Clustering, a General Deep Learning Framework of Representation Learning
arxiv-2102-07472.creator: Si Lu 1, Ruisi Li
arxiv-2102-07472.description: Abstract Clustering performs an essential role in many real world applications, such as market research, pattern recognition, data analysis, and image processing. However, due to the high dimensionality of the input feature values, the data being fed to clustering algorithms usually contains noise and thus could lead to in-accurate clustering results.

arxiv-2110-02157.title: Double Inozemtsev Limits of the Quantum DELL System
arxiv-2110-02157.creator: Alexander Gorsky, Peter Koroteev, Olesya Koroteeva, Shamil Shakirov
arxiv-2110-02157.description: Abstract . In this letter we study various Inozemtsev-type limits of the quantum double elliptic (DELL) system when both elliptic parameters are sent to zero at different rates, while the coupling constant is sent to infinity, such that a certain combination of the three parameters is kept fixed.

arxiv-2202-01024.title: Microfluidic osmotic compression of a charge-stabilized colloidal dispersion: Equation of state and collective diffusion coefficient
arxiv-2202-01024.creator: Camille Keita 1, Yannick Hallez 2, Jean-Baptiste Salmon 1
arxiv-2202-01024.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Camille Keita 1, Yannick Hallez 2, Jean-Baptiste Salmon 1. We show, using a model coupling mass transport and liquid theory calculations for a charge-stabilized colloidal dispersion, that diffusion significantly limits measurement times of its Equation Of State (EOS), osmotic pressure vs composition, using the osmotic compression technique. Following this result, we present a microfluidic chip allowing one to measure the entire EOS of a charged dispersion at the nanoliter scale in a few hours.

arxiv-2202-02696.title: Surface Slices and Homology spheres
arxiv-2202-02696.creator: Clayton McDonald
arxiv-2202-02696.description: Abstract . Here we develop the theory of the diagrammatics of surface cross sections to prove that there are an infinite number of homology 3-spheres smoothly embeddable in a homology 4-sphere but not in a homotopy 4-sphere. Our primary obstruction comes from work of Daemi. 1.

arxiv-2205-10836.title: On the Price of Fairness of Allocating Contiguous Blocks
arxiv-2205-10836.creator: Ankang Sun Bo Li
arxiv-2205-10836.description: Abstract In this work, we study the problem of fairly allocating a number of indivisible items that are located on a line to multiple agents. A feasible allocation requires that the allocated items to each agent are connected on the line. The items can be goods on which agents have non-negative utilities, or chores on which the utilities are non-positive.

arxiv-2206-10563.title: Experimental verification of the area law of mutual information in a quantum field simulator
arxiv-2206-10563.creator: Mohammadamin Tajik, Ivan Kukuljan, Spyros Sotiriadis, Bernhard Rauer, Thomas Schweigler, Federica Cataldini, João Sabino, Frederik Møller, Philipp Schüttelkopf, Si-Cong Ji, Dries Sels, Eugene Demler, Jörg Schmiedmayer
arxiv-2206-10563.description: Abstract Theoretical understanding of the scaling of entropies and the mutual information has led to significant advances in the research of correlated states of matter, quantum field theory, and gravity. Measuring von Neumann entropy in quantum many-body systems is challenging as it requires complete knowledge of the density matrix.

arxiv-2306-03049.title: WHO-IS: Wireless Hetnet Optimization using Impact Selection
arxiv-2306-03049.creator: Thomas Sandholm, Irene Macaluso, Sayandev Mukherjee
arxiv-2306-03049.description: Abstract We propose a method to first identify users who have the most negative impact on the overall network performance, and then offload them to an orthogonal channel. The feasibility of such an approach is verified using real-world traces, network simulations, and a lab experiment that employs multi-homed wireless stations.

arxiv-2410-13921.title: Epidemic waves for a two-group SIRS model with double nonlocal effects in a patchy environment 1 1 1 Research supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 12071074) and Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (No. 2023A1515012078).
arxiv-2410-13921.creator: Chufen Wu, Yonghui Xia, Jianshe Yu
arxiv-2410-13921.description: Abstract Abstract: We propose a lattice dynamical system that arises in a discrete diffusive two-group epidemic model with latency in a patchy environment. The model considers the SIS form and latency of the disease in group 1, while the SIR form without latency of the disease in group 2.

arxiv-2505-01514.title: Securing the Future of IVR: AI-Driven Innovation with Agile Security, Data Regulation, and Ethical AI Integration
arxiv-2505-01514.creator: Khushbu Mehboob Shaikh, Georgios Giannakopoulos
arxiv-2505-01514.description: Abstract The rapid digitalization of communication systems has elevated Interactive Voice Response (IVR) technologies to become critical interfaces for customer engagement. With Artificial Intelligence (AI) now driving these platforms, ensuring secure, compliant, and ethically designed development practices is more imperative than ever.

arxiv-2507-19557.title: JOINT FEATURE AND OUTPUT DISTILLATION FOR LOW-COMPLEXITY ACOUSTIC SCENE CLASSIFICATION
arxiv-2507-19557.description: Abstract This report presents a dual-level knowledge distillation framework with multi-teacher guidance for low-complexity acoustic scene classification (ASC) in DCASE2025 Task 1. We propose a distillation strategy that jointly transfers both soft logits and intermediate feature representations. Specifically, we pre-trained PaSST and CP-ResNet models as teacher models.

pmc-10590519.title: Triglyceride-glucose index is associated with severe obstructive coronary artery disease and atherosclerotic target lesion failure among young adults
pmc-10590519.creator: Shalaimaiti Shali, Lingfeng Luo, Kang Yao, Xiangdong Sun, Hongyi Wu, Shuning Zhang, Lili Xu, Wei Gao, Jianxuan Li, Juying Qian, Yan Zheng, Yuxiang Dai, Junbo Ge, the GRAND investigators
pmc-10590519.description: BackgroundEarly diagnosis and treatment effectiveness of early-onset coronary artery disease (EOCAD) are crucial, and non-invasive predictive biomarkers are needed for young adults. We aimed to evaluate the usefulness of the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a novel marker of insulin resistance, in identifying young CAD patients and predicting their risk of developing target lesion failure (TLF).

pmc-11328797.title: Latent transition analysis on post-traumatic stress and post-traumatic growth among firefighters
pmc-11328797.creator: Yongchan Shin, JeeEun Karin Nam, Minho Park, Aeyoung Lee, Youngkeun Kim
pmc-11328797.description: Background: Firefighters, in the course of their professional responsibilities, confront an array of stressors contingent upon the distinctive characteristics of their duties.Objective: This study investigated the longitudinal impact of trauma incidents during duty on firefighters using latent transition analysis.Method: Data from 346 firefighters in South Korea who had experienced trauma events while on duty were utilized.

pmc-11412119.title: Effect of librarian collaboration on otolaryngology systematic review and meta-analysis quality
pmc-11412119.creator: Rachel Whitney, Michael C. Shih, Tamar Gordis, Shaun A. Nguyen, Ted A. Meyer, Emily A. Brennan
pmc-11412119.description: Objective:To determine if librarian collaboration was associated with improved database search quality, search reproducibility, and systematic review reporting in otolaryngology systematic reviews and meta-analyses.Methods:In this retrospective cross-sectional study, PubMed was queried for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published in otolaryngology journals in 2010, 2015, and 2021. Two researchers independently extracted data.

pmc-11709792.title: Extending Molecular Subtyping in Alzheimer’s using Machine Learning Techniques and Alternative Splicing Data
pmc-11709792.creator: Lewis Edward Palmer
pmc-11709792.description: BackgroundRecent studies suggest the existence of distinct molecular subtypes within the AD patient cohort, characterized by distinct gene expression patterns in AD‐relevant genes and pathways. Understanding these putative subtypes may prove pivotal to the greater understanding of AD pathology and developing targeted therapeutic interventions.

pmc-11860565.title: Evidence-Informed Approach to De-Prescribing of Atypical Antipsychotics (AAP) in the Management of Behavioral Expressions (BE) in Advanced Neurocognitive Disorders (NCD): Results of a Retrospective Study
pmc-11860565.creator: A. S. Luthra, R. LinBin Gao, P. Carducci, J. Sue, S. Remers
pmc-11860565.description: IntroductionDiagnosis of behaviors in advanced neurocognitive disorders (aNCD) is one of exclusion, and the framework has been laid out in DSM-V. However, clinical assessments in aNCD become increasingly unreliable, and commonly used psychometric tools for clinical assessments lack reliability and validity, thereby making outcomes unreliable.

pmc-12418644.title: Production, optimization and characterization of esterase isolated from a new endophytic Trichoderma afroharzianum strain AUMC 16,433 and its applications in dye decolorization
pmc-12418644.creator: Yehia A -G Mahmoud, Nisrin S Alamin, Tarek M Mohamed, Nesma A El-Zawawy, Maha M Salem
pmc-12418644.description: Background and aimSynthetic dyes in the textile industry pose risks to human health and environmental safety. The current study aims to examine the efficacy of a novel esterase derived from an endophyte fungus in decolorizing diverse dyes, focusing on its production, purification, optimization, and characterization.

pmc-12484331.title: Pharmacotherapy for Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis
pmc-12484331.creator: Stéphane Jouneau, Pierre Chauvin, Mathieu Lederlin, Benoît Painvin, Mallorie Kerjouan
pmc-12484331.description: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is suspected when a “crazy paving” pattern is observed on a chest CT scan. This diagnosis is confirmed by the presence of eosinophilic extracellular material that shows positive staining with Periodic Acid Schiff on bronchoalveolar lavage samples. The autoimmune form of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is confirmed by detecting anti-granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor antibodies in the patient’s serum.

pmc-13127077.title: Delayed Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia After Remission in Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
pmc-13127077.creator: Nicholas Azinge, Tigabu Bishaw, Raghav Veluri, Mekdem Bisrat, Anand Deonarine, Ahmed Ali
pmc-13127077.description: A 46-year-old man with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) in remission since 2014 presented with progressive dizziness, fatigue, and dark-colored urine. Laboratory workup revealed hemoglobin levels of 5.9 g/dL, elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), hyperbilirubinemia, low haptoglobin, and a positive direct Coombs test for IgG, C3, and poly-specific antibodies, confirming warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA).

pmc-13321411.creator: Xingyu Lu, Dehuan Xie, Liang Cui, Hang Shang, Linghong Zhou

pmc-13472810.title: Platform compliance governance in digital public health communication: effects of emergency health knowledge dissemination on protective behaviors
pmc-13472810.creator: Qing Lu, Haotian Chen, Yi Jiang, Shuhui Li, Shuaishuai Cao
pmc-13472810.description: BackgroundDigital health information platforms have become important channels for public health science communication and emergency prevention knowledge. However, uncertainty about content accuracy, information disclosure, privacy protection, and communication behavior may weaken public trust and reduce the conversion of health knowledge into protective behavior.

pmc-13583549.title: Disulfiram Attenuates Adenine‐Induced Renal Fibrosis by Modulating Inflammatory and Immunometabolic Responses
pmc-13583549.creator: Saori Kin, Yuji Oe, Shun Ishigaki, Ichiro Fujio, Mariko Miyazaki, Tetsuhiro Tanaka
pmc-13583549.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is partly driven by excessive innate immune activation, which contributes to progressive renal injury and fibrosis. Disulfiram (DSF), an approved treatment for alcohol dependence, has recently emerged as an inhibitor of innate immune responses such as pyroptosis. In this study, we investigated whether DSF attenuates kidney injury in adenine‐induced nephropathy and explored the underlying mechanisms.
